div.head: Quadr II Praef 6
div.ab: Et licet inmeritos diuina tamen miseratio tanta prosequitur et tali dominos informatione componit, ne uilis aliquos seruitus adnichilet aut inpunita securitas elata precipitet; reges etiam, qui perfunctoria ceteros pompa preueniunt, ne potentatibus insolescant, carnis infirmitatibus et humanis admodum necessitatibus expositos utili penitus sollicitatione frequentat.
div.note: New row (October 2026): Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 543 (two independent readings of the page images, differences settled against the page)
div.ab: And although they are undeserving, the divine mercy yet attends them so greatly and orders the lords with such instruction, lest vile servitude bring some to nothing or unpunished security cast down the exalted; kings also, who go before others with passing pomp, lest they grow insolent in their powers, it visits with a thoroughly useful disquiet, exposed as they are to the infirmities of the flesh and very much to human necessities.

note.seg: die adligen Dynasten; vgl. o. S. 533l
the noble magnates; cf. above p. 533 note l

seg.hi: Verf. begrüsst das persönliche Leid des Königs nur im seelsorgerischen, nicht etwa im antiroyalistischen Sinne

note.seg: the author welcomes the king's personal suffering only in a pastoral sense, not at all in an anti-royalist one
